target_customer: Application developers wanting machine learning without building models
problem: Developers had to build and tune machine learning models themselves; Marft let them upload data via web or API and receive an optimized embeddable model in their chosen language.
business_model: Developer API and model generation service, pricing not found

technical_complexity.rationale: Automatically generating optimized, embeddable models across languages from arbitrary data is hard for a three-person team.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network effects described; hosted ML APIs were being built by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found for Marft. Competitor information from before the batch was not found.

market_need_then: Not documented in sources found; machine learning as a service was an emerging category in 2012 to 2013.

branding.domain_note: marft.com redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, so the domain is parked.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Marft was a three-person Winter 2012 YC company building embeddable machine learning models for developers. The YC directory lists it as inactive and the domain is now a for-sale parking page. The cause of its end is not public: no acquisition, shutdown note, funding or customer information was found, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: YC page lists no founder names. Outcome, funding, competitor and branding searches returned nothing about Marft. Competitor sources found (a March 2013 blog on ML as a service naming Wise.io, BigML, Google Prediction API) are about a year after the batch and were not listed. Crunchbase and CB Insights profile contents were not opened.
